title: Altair Aether
note: Our own design: a ~300 kg lunar communications relay, fired off a mass driver near the lunar south pole into an elliptical frozen lunar orbit, built from real flight hardware where it exists. Frame: x along the track (the direction of travel, and the craft's axis: the launch load runs down it), z up, y left. The craft's separation plane is at x = 0; the sled and the rails are behind and below it. Pass 1: structure, tank, main thruster, sled and rails. Pass 2: propulsion (eight 1 N thrusters, latch valve, fill and drain valves, lines).

open_questions: Launch geometry: a shot from near the south pole puts the orbit's high point over the launch site only if the shot is near-vertical (about 2.1 km/s), not the 1.68 km/s horizontal shot the 14 g was worked out for. A horizontal shot from the south puts the high point over the north. Options: a track on a steep slope, a launch site further north, or a bigger burn to turn the orbit. The craft's structure is the same either way; the tank size here covers the vertical case.
Lunar Pathfinder's orbit differs between SSTL's guide (673 x 7331 km, 54.9°) and a 2022 NASA slide (500 x 7500 km, 57.8°); SSTL calls its values indicative.
A south-pole launch site reaches inclinations near 90° directly; the 54.9° orbit needs a site at or below about 55°S, or a plane change.
Propulsion has no filter or pressure transducer yet (no sourced part found); the thruster layout is our own, not copied from a flown craft.
